title: Choose Kitty's new visual world
question: A full replacement world. The roll assigned The Risograph Press; two challengers beat it on both axes. Keep the assigned, take a challenger, take the pick, re-roll, or take the category standard.

options.label: The Risograph Press
options.lineage: DIY riso print studios, indie zines and gig flyers
options.thesis: GitHub's rising week hand-pulled as a two-ink riso zine: every repo a numbered entry in this issue, this week's top mover overprinted as the cover block.
options.viewport: Standard shell — left rail styled as the zine's section list, range + filter bar, the ranked issue list as numbered entries with a language spot-ink tick; a press colophon strip prints source and time.
options.signature: The active language's spot ink floods the selection, and the top mover gets a misregistered poster block pinned above the list.
options.risk: Halftone texture and overprint must never touch the body text; misread, it costs legibility on a list you scan daily.

raised.raise: The ink set is fixed at three and every color does a real job: language identity, selection state, top-mover mark.
Every number (stars, forks, rank, age) set only in tabular monospace figures.

options.label: The Character Shelf
options.lineage: character-goods catalogs — a ranked cast on pastel grounds
options.thesis: Every repo a character ranked on a shelf: a name plate, a birthday (its created date) and a one-line personality note (its description), with the language as its ribbon color.
options.viewport: Left rail of language 'shelves'; a ranked roster where each entry carries a name plate, a one-line note, and a ribbon whose color is its language; the active entry takes its ribbon.
options.signature: Focus bounces the entry and lights its ribbon; delisted or low-ranked characters print desaturated.
options.case: The one-liner maps straight onto the repo description, and the whole world reads as warm and lived-in — the most on-brand with Kitty's character.
options.risk: Mascot kitsch buries the description unless the personality one-liner is given real space and type weight.

options.label: The Split-Flap Board
options.thesis: The trending list is a departure board: fixed columns (rank, repo, language, stars), and when data refreshes, changed fields cascade like split-flaps while rows rerank in place.
options.viewport: A ruled board with fixed columns and a header; language as the board's 'departure groups'; a status strip printing source, time, and any rate-limit delay in amber.
options.signature: On refresh, only the changed cells flip character-by-character and the row holds an amber highlight until seen — you watch the list rerank in place.
options.case: It is literally a sortable ranked table, so product clarity is native, and rerank-in-place is the honest way to show a list that moved.
options.risk: Flap motion on every refresh becomes noise; it must be bounded to changed cells only, and skipped under reduced motion.

options.label: The Cassette Insert
options.lineage: hand-inked cassette j-cards, timed a side at a time
options.thesis: An issue as a mixtape: ranges as Side A (daily) and Side B (week/month), repos as numbered tracks ruled in ballpoint with their running times (repo age).
options.viewport: A folded j-card: spine as the active language, a tracklist the ranked repos, running times right-aligned; sides flip with a y-axis turn.
options.signature: Flipping ranges is a physical side-flip, and a needle marker runs the active position down the inked tracklist.
options.case: Warm, handmade, and devs of a certain era know it by heart; a tracklist is a genuinely clean list.
options.risk: Shoehorning three ranges into two sides is arbitrary, and the hand-inked type can read as a costume over a data tool.

options.label: The Language Programme
options.thesis: The shell re-identifies to the active language's own brand: the selected language's official mark and hue take over the header and rail.
options.viewport: A neutral, instantly legible working screen whose identity is borrowed from the selected language; the language name set in that language's own brand character.
options.signature: Selecting a language morphs the shell's hue and mark — the product's organizing axis becomes the color system.
options.risk: The most on-product, therefore the most familiar landing; per-language brand hues can clash if not mediatized toward one working ground.

options.label: Re-roll
options.line: Deals a new assigned direction and a fresh set of challengers; everything shown above is eliminated.

options.label: The category standard
options.thesis: What a trending browser always ships — neutral rail plus ranked list, one blue accent — executed at full craft.
options.risk: Indistinguishable from the competition by design.

demoted.line: flat metro typographic tiles — loses clarity (giant cropped type fights a dense repo list).
demoted.kept: Total, unhedged color commitment: one accent owns every live state.

demoted.line: orienteering map — a map is not a ranked list.
demoted.kept: A fixed, meaningful color language where hue is data, never decoration.

demoted.line: botanical folio of life-stages — a folio is not a daily list.
demoted.kept: One exact scale and ground across every entry; calm, ruled rhythm.
